keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws Legnica's 5,150 km2 shape (with 17 cells of the Wrocław duchy, Wrocław and Środa Śląska) only from 1305, but the page has Henry V duke of Wrocław from 1290 ('The Lower Silesian duchies of Legnica and Wrocław were re-reunited until 1311'). Towns left in 1291 (to Bolko I of Jawor: Świdnica, Ziębice, Ząbkowice Śląskie, Strzelin) and 1294 (to Henry III of Głogów) are outside this outline. The Duchy of Silesia dossier keeps its own Wrocław shape to 1304, so the two overlap. Repair pass: Henry V's grant of Świdnica, Ziębice, Ząbkowice and Strzelin to Bolko I in 1291 (Henry V page) is not drawn here: that land is in no Legnica outline, and the Silesia dossier carries it (loss to Jawor in 1290, confidence 2) with the matching Jawor gain of 1291, so this dossier has no 1291 loss.

5,150 km2 (23 cells). Holds for 1305-1310. The page: 'in 1311 Lower Silesia was split again, with Wrocław going to his younger brother Henry VI the Good' (the infobox lists the split of the Duchy of Brzeg as 1311); Wrocław and Środa Śląska are 17 of the shape's 23 cells, so the new keyframe _1311 draws the shape without them for 1311-1313. region.text: the Legnica and Jawor lands of Cliopatria's 1279 shapes

ledger.note: 1248: Bolesław II the Bald founds the Duchy of Legnica. The infobox gives 'Partitioned from the Duchy of Wrocław: 1248'; the text says Legnica 'from 1248 was the seat of a principality in its own right' and the lead that it was ruled by 'a local line of the Piast dynasty between 1248 and 1675'. The page names no borders.

minus.text: the Legnica and Jawor lands of Cliopatria's 1279 shapes

region.text: the northern Głogów lands of Konrad I, without the Lubusz strip sold in 1248-1249 and without the Legnica lands

ledger.note: 1251: Bolesław II pays his brother Konrad off with the new Duchy of Głogów. Konrad's claim 'had to be paid off by Bolesław with the newly created Duchy of Głogów in 1251'; the infobox lists the Głogów split as 1251.

1274: Jawor is split off Legnica. Infobox: 'Split off Duchy of Jawor: 1274'; the Jawor page: 'established in 1274 as a subdivision of the Duchy of Legnica'. The Henry V page has Henry given Jawor by his father in 1273.

1277: Środa Śląska and Strzegom pass to Legnica. 'In 1277, the towns of Środa Śląska and Strzegom passed from the Duchy of Wrocław to the Duchy of Legnica.' The Henry V page: Henry acquired Środa 'in exchange for the release of Henry IV' in 1277 and kept it. The Silesia dossier reads the payment as 'end of year 1277-78'.

region.text: the 17 cells of Cliopatria's 1305 Legnica shape that lie in its Duchy of Silesia (Wrocław) shape: Wrocław and Środa Śląska

ledger.note: 1290: Henry V becomes Duke of Wrocław. 'Henry V defeated his cousin Henry Probus and succeeded him as duke of Wrocław in 1290'; after Probus died on 23 June 1290 the people of Wrocław 'invited Henry V to assume the throne', though Henry III of Głogów 'had been named successor but refused to abdicate' (Henry V page). Cliopatria draws only 17 cells of the duchy with Legnica, from 1305. Repair pass: Henry V's 1291 grant of the Świdnica towns to Bolko I of Jawor was dropped from this ledger as a loss because no Legnica keyframe draws that land; the Silesia dossier (1290) and Jawor (1291) carry it.

region.text: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus, whose people invited Henry V to rule after 23 June 1290

ledger.note: July 1290: Henry III of Głogów contests Wrocław. After Probus's death 'Henry III of Głogów had been named successor but refused to abdicate'; the Głogów dossier reads his declaration of war on Henry V from the Henry III page. The first campaign is not described.

region.text: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus, whose people invited Henry V to rule after 23 June 1290

ledger.note: November 1293: Henry V is captured and the war for Wrocław ends in his defeat. He was 'betrayed on 11 November 1293' and 'imprisoned for about six months'.

region.text: Namysłów, Bierutów, Oleśnica, Kluczbork and Bolesławiec

ledger.note: 1294: Henry V buys his freedom with towns. He was freed 'by ceding towns to Henry III, including Namysłów, Bierutów, Oleśnica, Kluczbork and Bolesławiec, and paying a ransom of 30,000 pieces'. The Duchy of Głogów page puts the Głogów gains of Oleśnica, Bolesławiec and Chojnów in 1296; the Henry V page puts the cession after the captivity of about six months from 11 November 1293.

ledger.counterpart: Duchy of Wrocław of Henry VI the Good (1311-1335)
ledger.note: 1311: Lower Silesia is split again and Wrocław goes to Henry VI the Good. 'In 1311 Lower Silesia was split again, with Wrocław going to his younger brother Henry VI the Good' (Legnica page); the infobox lists the split of the Duchy of Brzeg as 1311. The Henry VI page: 'the Duchy was divided into three parts: Wrocław, Legnica and Brzeg' and 'Henry was allowed to take Wrocław'; he ruled the Duchy of Wrocław to his death on 24 November 1335 and by the treaty of 1327 it passed to the Bohemian crown. The counterpart is not duchy-of-silesia, which ends in 1304; Henry VI's duchy has no dossier. Cliopatria keeps the Wrocław cells with Legnica to 1313; keyframe _1311 draws the shape without them.

ledger.note: 1313: the last Cliopatria shape of the Duchy of Legnica. The duchy itself lasted to 1675 ('In 1329 he had to pay homage to the Bohemian King John of Luxembourg'; Bolesław III ruled again 1312-1342). Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bohemia covers the land from 1314; the year is the map's, the page is silent.

wars.name: Wrocław-Legnica dispute of 1277
wars.outcome: Środa Śląska and Strzegom passed from Wrocław to Legnica in 1277; the Henry V page ties the acquisition of Środa to 'the release of Henry IV'.
wars.note: The pages opened name no battle; the Silesia dossier has the capture at Jelcz and the battle of Stolec (24 April 1277) from other pages.

wars.name: War for the Duchy of Wrocław (Henry V the Fat against Henry III of Głogów)

zones.text: the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry IV Probus, whose people invited Henry V to rule after 23 June 1290

wars.outcome: After Henry IV Probus died (23 June 1290) Wrocław invited Henry V; Henry III of Głogów refused to abdicate. Henry V was betrayed and captured on 11 November 1293 and freed after about six months by ceding Namysłów, Bierutów, Oleśnica, Kluczbork and Bolesławiec and paying 30,000 pieces; he held Wrocław until the split of 1311.

certainty.note: The duchy's frontiers are lists of towns and castellanies; the pages give no treaty boundary.

notes: Cliopatria's Legnica row begins in 1279 although the duchy began in 1248; the Legnica and Jawor lands are drawn inside Cliopatria's Duchy of Głogów outline for 1250-1278, which the Głogów dossier corrects; this dossier supplies keyframes _1248 and _1274 for them. The Wrocław duchy: the page has Henry V duke of Wrocław from 1290 to 1311; Cliopatria keeps a Duchy of Silesia (Wrocław) shape to 1304 and gives Legnica 17 of its cells from 1305; the two dossiers overlap in 1290-1304 (Silesia 80 cells, Legnica's _1290 keyframe 23 cells). Dates that disagree: Jawor granted 1273 (Henry V page) or split off 1274 (infobox); Środa Śląska 1277 (Legnica page) or end of 1277-78 (Silesia dossier); the 1294 ransom towns against 1296 on the Głogów page; guardianship of Henry V's sons by Bolko I (Henry V page) or King Wenceslaus (Legnica page). The Brzeg duchy (split 1311, infobox) lies outside the Cliopatria shape. The duchy outlived the map (Bohemian vassal 1329, Habsburg 1675); the additions batch eu-15-x is to cover the Polish duchies after 1304. Gazetteer lacks Legnica, Środa Śląska, Strzegom, Namysłów, Bierutów, Oleśnica, Kluczbork, Bolesławiec (circles by coordinates, from the towns, not from the pages). Counterparts without a dossier: none beyond the Wrocław duchy (inside duchy-of-silesia). Repair pass of 2026-10-31 (reviewer findings): the 1305 shape is cut to 1305-1310 and keyframe _1311 draws it without the 17 Wrocław cells; the 1311 loss names the Duchy of Wrocław of Henry VI the Good (1311-1335; needs a dossier, since duchy-of-silesia ends in 1304 and Cliopatria's 'Duchy of Wrocław' row ends in 1201); the 1291 loss of the Świdnica towns is dropped because no Legnica keyframe draws that land (Silesia 1290 and Jawor 1291 carry it); who draws Wrocław in 1290-1304 (Legnica _1290 against the Silesia shape) remains for the orchestrator.
